statement: Create a jewellery chain by repeating a link along guide curves with correct link spacing and alternating orientation.
superiority: Dino 8 should add link collision checking and automatic closure so chains are printable and wearable.

acceptance.corpus: Oval link 8 x 5 mm, 40 links along a 300 mm closed guide curve
acceptance.tolerance: Link pitch error < 0.05 mm; no link interpenetration (intersection volume 0); closure gap < 0.01 mm

notes: Identity check: on Food4Rhino and McNeel pages Peacock is a free parametric jewellery framework for Grasshopper by Daniel Abalde, not a fractal or L-system tool.

statement: Build a gem railing: a rail that holds a row of stones along a curve with seats cut to each stone size.
superiority: Dino 8 should size seats from standard gem tables and show wall thickness live.

acceptance.corpus: 20 round brilliant stones 1.5 mm diameter along a 40 mm curve
acceptance.tolerance: Seat diameter equals stone girdle within 0.02 mm; minimum wall >= 0.3 mm everywhere

notes: Identity check: on Food4Rhino and McNeel pages Peacock is a free parametric jewellery framework for Grasshopper by Daniel Abalde, not a fractal or L-system tool.

statement: Set stones with prongs (claws) and cutter geometry so the setting can be subtracted from the metal body.
superiority: Dino 8 should include a setting library with checks for prong height, spacing and stone retention.

acceptance.corpus: 4-prong setting for a 6.5 mm round stone
acceptance.tolerance: Prong spacing symmetric within 0.01 mm; cutter volume subtraction yields a valid closed solid

notes: Identity check: on Food4Rhino and McNeel pages Peacock is a free parametric jewellery framework for Grasshopper by Daniel Abalde, not a fractal or L-system tool.

statement: Parameterize jewellery templates and elements (shank, head, gem, claws, clasps, halo) so a design can be varied by changing parameters instead of editing finished geometry.

source.ref: Parametric jewellery elements and template library (roadmap)

superiority: Dino 8 should ship a template library with presets for ring sizes and standards and keep model history editable.

acceptance.corpus: Ring template swept over sizes US 4 to 13
acceptance.tolerance: Inner diameter equals the size table within 0.05 mm for all 10 sizes; every variant a valid solid

notes: Identity check: on Food4Rhino and McNeel pages Peacock is a free parametric jewellery framework for Grasshopper by Daniel Abalde, not a fractal or L-system tool. Library listed as planned in the release thread.

statement: Generate a collection of design variations automatically from one parametric design and compare them.
superiority: Dino 8 should provide a built-in variant generator with thumbnails and a bill of materials per variant.

acceptance.corpus: Ring template with 5 parameters, 3 values each (243 variants)
acceptance.tolerance: All variants generated in one run with identical results across 2 runs; each variant passes validity check

notes: Identity check: on Food4Rhino and McNeel pages Peacock is a free parametric jewellery framework for Grasshopper by Daniel Abalde, not a fractal or L-system tool.

statement: Check a jewellery model for manufacturability: minimum wall thickness, printability and repair of defects before casting or printing.

source.ref: Analysis, repair and printability tools (planned for 1.x)

superiority: Dino 8 should compute wall thickness exactly on the solid and offer one-click repair with a before-after report.

acceptance.corpus: Test solids with known thin walls of 0.2, 0.4, 0.8 mm
acceptance.tolerance: Reported minimum thickness within 0.01 mm; walls under 0.3 mm flagged 100 percent

notes: Identity check: on Food4Rhino and McNeel pages Peacock is a free parametric jewellery framework for Grasshopper by Daniel Abalde, not a fractal or L-system tool. This capability is listed as a roadmap item in the release thread.

statement: Control generative production: manage the geometry, costs, technical tables, renders and usage notes of a jewellery definition in one controller.
superiority: Dino 8 should link metal weight and cost to the model volume with alloy densities and export the technical sheet.

acceptance.corpus: Ring with known volume 950 mm3 in 18k gold (density about 15.5 g/cm3)
acceptance.tolerance: Computed weight within 0.5 percent of volume x density
